Subject: Dedicated pool question + workload summary

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is a short workbook with daily request volume (peaks and baselines), sample payloads, and token histograms. High level:
- Peak sustained requests: ~120 req/s for 2–3 hours/day (US morning)
- Baseline: 15–25 req/s outside peaks
- Average conversation context: 1,024 tokens (including system + user)
- Model mix: 60% 13B useful for short replies, 40% 70B for long-form tasks

Also, our security team will ask for an audit trail of inference logs retention options. Can you and Marcus propose pool sizing + a pricing pathway (starter commit vs full commit) and expected unit economics?

Thanks,

Sam — thanks for the workbook, that helps a lot. I looped in Marcus (solutions) and Lauren (AE) to scope a recommendation. High level summary and ask:

1) Quick recommendation (ballpark):
- Suggested committed pool: 8x H100-equivalent GPUs (mixed-precision + quantized 70B path)
- Throughput expectation: ~120 req/s sustained with a 20% headroom for spikes (burst pool handles short bursts)
- Concurrency: handles ~48 concurrent active sessions at peak with avg 1,024 token contexts and an average response length ~160 tokens
- Token throughput: ~2.1–2.6M tokens/day under your profile

2) Pricing path options (examples):
- Starter commit (6mo): 4x GPUs, 15% commit discount, uplifts for burst credits, no SLA-backed latency guarantee (best-effort)
- Production commit (24mo recommended): 8x GPUs, 20–25% commit discount depending on ARR and payment terms, 99.9% availability SLA and p95/p99 latency targets for the committed baseline

3) Burst and fallback behavior:
- Burst pool available up to +40% for short windows (metered usage billed overage or via pre-purchased burst credits)
- Automatic fallback to quantized 13B variants if the 70B pool is saturated for non-latency-critical requests

4) Security / logs: we retain inference-level audit logs for up to 12 months by default for Dedicated; longer retention is an add-on. We can provide an SOC2 artifact and KMS integration notes.

Action items: Marcus will provide detailed throughput modeling and a recommended GPU mix (H100 vs A100/Q) plus expected cost per token; Lauren will prepare a pricing term sheet (starter vs production commit) and outline discount thresholds. I attached a draft pricing overview for internal reference.

—Olga

Following up with the workload sizing math and three capacity scenarios. I kept the external recipients on copy so Sam/Priya can see assumptions.

Assumptions: average model latency (token generation) and kernel perf measured on H100-class instances, steady-state request distribution from your sheet.

Scenario A — Starter (conservative)- 4x H100- Estimated sustained throughput: ~60–70 req/s (good for baseline + small peaks)- p95 latency (13B/70B mix): ~230ms / ~520ms respectively at target concurrency- Risk: spikes will push to overage/burst quickly

Scenario B — Balanced (recommended minimal prod)- 6x H100- Sustained throughput: ~95–110 req/s with ~15% headroom- p95 latency: ~180ms (13B) / ~380ms (70B)- Much lower reliance on burst credits, good for 8–12hr daily peaks

Scenario C — High-assurance (full commit)- 8x H100 (recommended for your worst-case peak)- Sustained throughput: ~130–150 req/s with 20–30% headroom- p95 latency: ~160ms (13B) / ~320ms (70B); p99 targets depend on model eviction and KV cache warmness but we can specify 99th latency SLAs for committed baseline

Notes on concurrency and caching:
- With 1,024 token contexts and an average response of 160 tokens, the dominant cost is decoder token throughput. KV cache reuse across sessions (where applicable) improves effective throughput for multi-turn flows by ~12–18%.
- If Polaris can route long-form generation to a slightly delayed worker (background job) we can shift load away from the low-latency pool and reduce needed GPUs by ~1–2 units.

Sizing recommendation: pick Scenario C if you need hard guarantees during the daily peak and want to avoid frequent burst consumption. Scenario B is an acceptable cost/latency compromise if you can tolerate occasional brief slower responses during sustained unexpected load.

I'll attach the perf model snapshot and cost per GPU baseline; Lauren, can you draft the term sheet against Scenario C with a 24mo commit and a 20% discount baseline + volume kicker at ARR milestones?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Recommended commitment: 8x H100, 24-month term- Base commit discount: 20% off list monthly capacity rate- Milestone kicker: additional 3% discount when ARR crosses $750k in committed spend in year 1; 5% at $1.5M- Burst credits: 250 GPU-hours included per month, then metered at 0.8x on-demand rate- Credits & onboarding: one-time $15k professional services credit to help optimize batching, caching, and quantization profiles- SLA: 99.9% availability for committed baseline; p95/p99 latency SLOs will be defined in the MSA; rebates for missed targets capped at 3 months' credits

Next steps:
1) If you want to proceed, sign the attached term sheet and we’ll issue an initial PO for the ramp month.
2) Marcus to run a short lab test (2–3 days) on a subset of your payloads to validate p95 numbers before provisioning.
3) Security: we will start the SOC2 artifact exchange and confirm log retention or extended retention pricing.

Sam — any final questions on burst credits or the milestone discount mechanics? If not, I’ll push the DocuSign for the 24mo Scenario C path with the 20% baseline discount.
